THE BLIZZARD RANT [Jontron on Blizzard taking down the Nostalrius Private Server]

Although I'm not a fan of the entire "Vanilla/TBC/WotLK" server crowd" (imho things would get stale eventually due to the lack of new content), I do agree with Jontron here in that the private server posed absolutely no risk to either Blizzard or WoW proper, especially since the entire project was free-of-cost. Hell, you could argue that more people might decide to come back to WoW proper after having played on such a Nostalgia server.

That being said, it's not like it still matters. WoW is dead in the water.

The thing that crowd is protesting though (and I happen to agree) is how the game mechanics got thrown in the shitter as more content came out. If the game froze mechanically on TBC/WotLK, or hell, even Cataclysm (Even though it was a step down, at least it still bore a semblance of the base game in it) a huge number of people from that crowd (including myself) would still be playing that game.

Honestly, one big thing that they missed out on that could have been the easiest "Content push" in the world was just scaling all of the old dungeons/raids up to the "New Level Cap" power level. They didn't need to completely redesign them or anything, but I mean, I can count the number of people I've run with who knew what to do for every part of Scholomance on my fingers and toes. Likewise with many of the older raids and dungeons. If Karazhan had a level 80 option during WOTLK I would have still taken a raid into that dungeon every single reset. However, because they DIDN'T do these things, I almost feel like often the expansions caused me to LOSE content - Going into BT and soloing all of the content in there just doesn't do it for me. Why must I lose that, and hyjal, sunwell, tempest keep, SSC, etc. just because WoTLK is out? Why must I lose ICC, TOTC, Naxx (reboot), etc. just because Cata is out? Why did I have to lose all of the vanilla content to TBC? Before you can make a claim that it'd get stale because the game never has any new content, I feel as though the content that's been lost to time needs to be addressed first. Sure, there's new content, but what about all of the old content that many players never even saw?

For me it all started with the whole Green > Purple nonsense with TBC. People worked for months to get to 60, then months longer to get those tier 5 and 6 items. In a flash, toons who couldn't even enter those raids because they were lvl 58 could go get better gear from quests/drops than many of the players who had spent a lot of time getting what they had.
